Thermal metamaterials enable precise manipulation of temperature fields by tuning thermal and structural parameters.
Passive temperature maintenance technologies include phase change materials, shape memory alloys, solar thermal utilization, sky radiation cooling, and heat pipe systems.
The energy-free thermostat uses temperature trapping theory and nonlinear thermal conductivity to maintain stable temperature without energy input.
Materials type-A and type-B in the energy-free thermostat have thermal conductivities defined by logistic functions dependent on temperature.
Shape memory alloys deform upon phase transition, enabling dynamic changes in thermal conductivity in composite structures.
Experimental results show the energy-free thermostat maintains central region temperature within 293.3–293.5 K despite varying ambient gradients.
The negative-energy thermostat combines thermotics with thermoelectric effects to generate electricity while maintaining temperature.
The thermoelectromotive force in the negative-energy thermostat is approximated by ΔU ≈ S(T2 − T1), where S is the Seebeck coefficient.
Finite element simulations confirm the negative-energy thermostat maintains stable temperature and increasing electric potential with larger ambient gradients.
The negative-energy thermostat remains effective under electrical loads with both low and high electrical and thermal conductivities.
The multi-temperature maintenance container uses adaptive controls and phase change materials to maintain multiple temperatures simultaneously.
Thermal metamaterials research began with conduction heat transfer and is expanding to convection and radiation heat transfer.
Effective medium theory is used to fabricate thermal metamaterials with designed thermal parameters not found in natural materials.
Thermal cloaks guide heat flow around objects, making them thermally invisible, and can be enhanced with energy-free thermostat concepts.
Maintaining zero net heat flow across a temperature control zone is essential for strict temperature maintenance and energy conservation.
The paper introduces three devices based on thermal metamaterials: energy-free thermostat, negative-energy thermostat, and multi-temperature maintenance container.
The energy-free thermostat design includes adiabatic boundaries on top and bottom and fixed high and low temperature boundaries on sides.
The negative-energy thermostat can be integrated into a thermoelectric cloak to simultaneously maintain temperature and regulate electrical potential.
The temperature trapping theory relies on creating steep temperature gradients outside a central zone to keep its temperature stable.
The practical realization of nonlinear thermal conductivity functions is achieved by combining stationary and movable components in composite materials.
